name: Green Valley Vistas
headline: Brikwell and the Denver Housing Authority plan Green Valley Vistas, 156 new apartments for households at 30% to 80% AMI, including 49 three- and four-bedroom homes and an early childhood education center, on 3.6 acres at 5000 Tower Road in Green Valley Ranch. It won a 2025 federal 4% credit award from CHFA, backed by City of Denver bonds.
why_it_matters: This is a layered public deal on former Denver Health land: a $4.75M Denver linkage-fee loan with a 99-year covenant, a $1.95M state grant, Denver bond cap topped up with just under $4M delegated by DHA, and DHA project-based vouchers. The bond issuance ordinance and the financial closing are the next things to watch.

status.label: Land bought (July 2026); bonds induced; financing not closed; construction not started
status.detail: DHA and Brikwell closed on the land by 2026-07-15 and said construction will start once financing and permits are complete. Denver approved the $4.75M loan on 2026-06-22 and the bond inducement on 2026-07-27. No bond issuance ordinance, financial closing or building permit was found as of 2026-10-21. The city loan must close by 2027-03-27.

next_step: Watch for a Denver bond issuance ordinance for Green Valley Vistas at the Finance and Business Committee, then the financial closing and a building permit.

key_numbers.value: 156 homes, all income-restricted (30% to 80% AMI, averaging 54% AMI)
key_numbers.meaning: 133 homes (85%) are at or below 60% AMI. The mix is 38 studios, 45 one-bedroom, 24 two-bedroom, 25 three-bedroom and 24 four-bedroom units.
About $26.8M over 10 years. No state credit.
The amount CHFA prints. Denver's inducement awards up to $27M of its bond cap, including just under $4M of cap that DHA is delegating to the city.

key_numbers.value: $4,750,000 Denver loan plus a $1,950,000 state grant
key_numbers.meaning: The city loan is a 1% cash-flow loan from linkage-fee money with a 99-year affordability covenant. The state grant is a May 2026 Division of Housing award.

facts.value: 5000 Tower Road, Denver 80249 (Green Valley Ranch, Council District 11)
Family, new construction. Not in a QCT or DDA, but in a SADDA. Section 8 column marked No.
About 3.6 acres (3.59 acres per the city), formerly owned by Denver Health

Two residential buildings, per DHA: one four stories with shared amenities, and one three stories with a 5,700 sq ft early childhood education center. About 175 parking spaces and a 3,500 sq ft park and playground.
The city's loan request says the project will partner with DHA and include project-based vouchers for families
Green Valley Vistas Owner, LLC, a Colorado limited liability company. It was the contract purchaser of the land when the loan agreement was signed.
99-year rental and occupancy covenant recorded at the city loan closing. All affordable units are floating.
At least 5% of units built accessible for people with mobility disabilities, plus another 2% under the loan agreement's accessibility terms

money.note: 2025 cycle. CHFA marks the amounts subject to change.

money.source: Tax-exempt private activity bonds (City and County of Denver, Department of Housing Stability)
money.amount: $21,000,000 per CHFA. The inducement allows up to $27,000,000.
money.note: Resolution CR26-0997, adopted 2026-07-27, awards up to $27M of Denver's bond cap, limited to the greater of 30% of eligible basis or the permanent loan amount. The award expires after one year unless extended. DHA is delegating just under $4M of its own bond cap to the city for the project. A final bond ordinance is still required.

money.source: City of Denver HOST loan (linkage fee)
money.note: 1% simple interest, repaid from cash flow starting about two years after the note date, and due at the 22nd anniversary. The request lists a 19-year term and names the Affordable Housing Fund as the source. The city will subordinate to senior debt of up to $52.5M. The loan agreement says the money helps finance the land purchase. Approved by Resolution CR26-0743 on 2026-06-22.

money.source: Colorado Division of Housing, State Housing Development Grant (vendor fee)
money.note: Shown as a rental award to Brikwell in the May 2026 round. Earlier requests were $4.5M in the October 2025 LOI round and $2.5M in the February 2026 round, the latter under the applicant name Green Valley Housing Partners.
DHA and Brikwell bought the land from Denver Health, closing by 2026-07-15. No price was disclosed.

background.text: Denver had planned a micro-community for people experiencing homelessness at 5000 Tower Road. On 2023-11-30 it dropped that plan, saying the site was not economically viable to develop because of land development costs.

DHA and Brikwell closed on the 3.6-acre site from Denver Health by 2026-07-15. DHA says the purchase enables housing for households at 30% to 80% AMI and that construction will start after financing and permitting.

Denver's Community Planning and Housing Committee approved the HOST loan by consent on 2026-06-02, and City Council adopted Resolution CR26-0743 on 2026-06-22. The loan agreement sets a closing deadline of 2027-03-27.

The Finance and Business Committee approved the bond inducement on 2026-07-14, and City Council adopted Resolution CR26-0997 on 2026-07-27. The resolution makes issuance subject to a bond purchase commitment, City approvals and design approval, and adoption of a final bond ordinance.

The city's loan request describes the project as family-oriented and focused on households below 60% AMI. It notes bus stops within two blocks, a light rail station within two miles, and elementary schools within a mile.
The loan agreement assigns each income band across bedroom sizes. For example, the 24 units at 30% AMI are 6 studios, 6 one-bedroom, 4 two-bedroom, 4 three-bedroom and 4 four-bedroom units.
Brikwell's development page lists Green Valley Vistas as 156 units financed with 4% LIHTC.

timeline.event: Denver cancels its planned micro-community at 5000 Tower Road
Brikwell files a $4.5M letter of intent with the Division of Housing
$2.5M Division of Housing application (Green Valley Housing Partners)
Division of Housing May 2026 round lists a $1,950,000 rental award to Brikwell
Denver City Council approves the $4.75M HOST loan (CR26-0743)
DHA announces that it and Brikwell have completed the land purchase from Denver Health
Denver City Council adopts the bond inducement for up to $27M (CR26-0997)
Listed on CHFA's Federal 4% award report under cycle year 2025
Deadline to close the city loan under the loan agreement

discrepancies.text: DHA describes two buildings, one four stories and one three stories, while the city's loan request describes a three-story, garden-style community.
The city's loan request and council summary give the loan a 19-year term, while the signed loan agreement makes it due on the 22nd anniversary of the promissory note.
The city's loan request says the project will include DHA project-based vouchers, while CHFA's award report marks the Section 8 column No.
DHA's release says the city contributed $4.75 million, while the city's records show a repayable cash-flow loan.
